edge: Distinguish L and H from unrestricted x and from a known value with multiple strength levels.
notes: Use set/range-aware oracles rather than requiring one implementation-selected member.
positive: Produce each ambiguous class through driver or switch combinations and inspect its permitted value/strength range.

edge: Combine ambiguous signals whose ranges remain entirely within one value portion and distinguish the resulting known-value range.
positive: Combine an H-range signal and an L-range signal whose bounds span both value portions and verify an x with the union's extreme bounds.

edge: Use opposite values so filtering creates a gap and verify intervening levels are restored.
positive: Combine an ambiguous range spanning above and below a known driver's strength and verify filtering at the known level.

edge: Verify z input produces x rather than propagating z through buf.
positive: Drive each four-state input value into buf and not and compare every output with the table.

edge: Create opposing or uncertain drivers whose result has an ambiguous multi-level strength and distinguish it from a single-strength result.
notes: Use detailed 28.12 requirements to construct drivers; this record scores the resulting strength-state form, not those algorithms again.
positive: Resolve a built-in net driven to a known value at one strength and inspect its single value/strength state.

edge: Exercise controls that enable both channels, neither channel, or an unknown channel.
positive: Compare a cmos instance with explicit parallel nmos and pmos instances over data and four-state control combinations.

edge: Compare x, H, and L transition timing and compare omitted delay with zero delay.
negative: Supply more than three CMOS delay values.
positive: Specify three distinct CMOS delays and observe rise, fall, and transition-to-z.

edge: Verify rcmos preserves small charge and high impedance.
notes: Hold CMOS control and data behavior constant while observing strength.
positive: Propagate a non-supply drive through cmos and verify preservation; propagate supply and verify strong.
Propagate strong, pull, and medium-charge signals through rcmos and verify the table reductions.

edge: Drive complementary controls to enable both component channels.
negative: Swap the n-channel and p-channel control terminals or omit one control.
positive: Instantiate cmos with output, input, n-control, and p-control in order.

edge: Use multiple unnamed instances in one comma-separated declaration.
negative: Attempt to place a distinct drive-strength or delay specification on the second instance in a comma-separated declaration.
positive: Declare two and instances after one drive-strength and delay specification and observe both with those declaration-wide settings.

edge: Compare a 2-state control with a 4-state control while holding pass terminals constant.
negative: Use an object outside the three permitted control categories as the control terminal.
positive: Control otherwise identical pass switches with a 4-state net, 4-state variable, and 2-state variable.

edge: On built-in nets, transition control to x or z and verify the smaller specified delay.
negative: Supply three delay values to tranif.
positive: Specify distinct turn-on and turn-off delays and toggle the pass-switch control.

negative: Place the control before either bidirectional terminal or provide the wrong terminal count.
positive: Instantiate each controlled pass-switch family with two inouts followed by a control.

edge: Compare omitted strength with an explicit `(strong1, strong0)` specification.
positive: Resolve an unspecified-strength gate output against a weaker driver and observe strong strength behavior.

edge: Use a transition to x whose delay is selected by a minimum rule.
positive: Apply otherwise identical value transitions at weak and supply input strengths and verify equal output timing.

edge: Use a multiple-output buf and verify the declaration strength governs each output terminal.
positive: Apply distinct explicit strengths to an eligible gate and observe the output strengths for 0 and 1.

edge: Exercise pullup and pulldown, whose strength forms differ from ordinary eligible gates.
negative: Attach a drive-strength specification to a tran or MOS switch.
positive: Apply a drive-strength specification to one primitive from each eligible gate family.

negative: Place the pair after the delay or omit its comma or parentheses.
positive: Use both `(strong1, weak0)` and reversed `(weak0, strong1)` forms before a delay.

edge: Reverse the two syntax members while preserving their 0/1 suffixes and verify unchanged value association.
positive: Use unequal strength0 and strength1 members and observe both output values.

edge: Compare the same value driven at weak and supply strengths against an opposing driver.
positive: Drive nets from gate and continuous-assignment outputs at each driving-strength class and observe strength-sensitive resolution.

negative: Specify `(highz0, highz1)` and `(highz1, highz0)` on an otherwise eligible gate.

edge: Repeat at supply strength and compare with unequal opposing strengths where the stronger driver wins.
positive: Combine weak0 and weak1 drivers and observe an x result with weak-or-lower ambiguity.

negative: Specify more than three delay values on such a gate.
notes: Primitive-family clauses can impose a smaller maximum.
positive: Use a legal three-value delay on a primitive form that permits rise, fall, and turn-off.

edge: Place a net delay after the gate and distinguish the two stages.
positive: Apply a gate input transition and observe the delayed output transition.

edge: Compare omitted delay, one explicit delay, and two equal delays across four-state source values.
notes: Remaining table rows complete from-to coverage.
positive: Exercise rise, fall, z, and x transitions with distinct two-value delays.

edge: Declare an unnamed primitive instance and a named arrayed instance in otherwise equivalent declarations.
negative: Give a tran primitive a drive-strength specification even though its grammar has no drive-strength slot.
notes: Vary one optional component or terminal category per case.
positive: Declare an and primitive with an output terminal and one or more input expressions, optionally naming the instance.

edge: Observe the H range's driven-1 bound and high-impedance endpoint.
positive: Compare otherwise identical unknown-output and gates using highz0 versus weak0 for the 0-output strength.

edge: Verify only the highz-designated logic value becomes z.
positive: Use highz1 with a non-highz strength0 and observe z instead of a driven 1.

edge: Use a one-element instance array and distinguish equal-width sharing from an invalid oversized partition.
negative: Connect an expression one bit too short or one bit too long for all array terminals.
positive: Connect an N×W-bit expression to N instances with W-bit terminals.

edge: Reference the right-hand and left-hand bound elements of a descending range.
negative: Reference a primitive array element using an index outside its declared range.
notes: Choose a portable observation that needs an individual hierarchical instance reference.
positive: Hierarchically reference a named primitive array element with an index inside its declared range.

edge: Use different mapping modes on separate terminals of the same instance array by varying expression widths.
positive: Connect a one-bit expression to a one-bit terminal across a multi-instance gate array and observe it shared by every instance.

edge: Use vectors whose declared direction is opposite the instance-array range direction.
notes: Combine with the detailed terminal-to-vector mapping rules that follow before materializing.
positive: Connect a primitive instance array to vectors and check that each instance maps to its corresponding indexed elements.

edge: Repeat with ascending and descending instance-array ranges; mapping is anchored to the right-hand index rather than the numerically smallest index.
positive: Connect a 16-bit expression to four instances having 4-bit terminals and verify the least-significant nibble reaches the right-hand-index instance.

edge: Use equal bounds and verify one array element is elaborated.
negative: Use a nonconstant expression as an instance-array bound.
positive: Declare arrays with ascending and descending nonzero constant bounds and check elaborated counts.

edge: Use a descending continuous range.
negative: Attach two ranges to one primitive instance identifier.
positive: Declare a named primitive array with one continuous packed-style index range.

edge: Contrast omitted range with an equal-bound range: both elaborate one instance, but only the latter is an array element.
positive: Declare a named primitive without a range and verify one scalar instance.

edge: Use a one-element array with a one-bit interconnect expression.
negative: Connect an interconnect expression whose width differs from the primitive array length.
positive: Connect an N-bit interconnect net expression to an N-element primitive instance array.

edge: Use expressions whose numerical values do not satisfy min ≤ typ ≤ max.
negative: Use other punctuation or omit one member of a min:typ:max triple.
notes: The selected member depends on the simulator's standardized timing-selection mode; do not assume the labels impose ordering.
positive: Specify independent min:typ:max triples for rise, fall, and turn-off delays.

edge: Cause a transition to x and verify use of the minimum applicable delay.
negative: Supply four delay values to an nmos declaration.
positive: Specify three distinct delays and observe rise, fall, and transition-to-z changes through an enabled MOS switch.

edge: Combine x and z controls with each four-state data value and verify H, L, x, or z outcomes.
notes: Use set-valued oracles for H and L.
positive: Exercise each MOS polarity with enabled and disabled controls and data 0 and 1.

notes: Use a set-aware value oracle while comparing event times.
positive: Use unequal transition delays and compare H, L, and x transition timing.

edge: Distinguish H and L from unrestricted x.
notes: Use a set-valued oracle for H and L.
positive: Use an unknown control combination that yields H or L and accept either member of its defined set.

edge: Compare resistive and nonresistive listed keywords while holding declaration shape applicable.
negative: Use tran as though it were a MOS switch declaration keyword.
positive: Declare each listed MOS switch keyword using its applicable terminal grammar.

edge: Verify a resistive MOS switch preserves small charge and high impedance.
notes: Hold polarity, control, and data constant while observing strength.
positive: Propagate ordinary and supply strengths through nmos or pmos and verify preservation versus supply-to-strong.
Propagate strong, pull, and medium-charge signals through rnmos or rpmos and verify table reductions.

edge: Use expressions for input and control while retaining a net lvalue output.
negative: Swap output and input terminal positions.
positive: Instantiate each unidirectional MOS switch with output, input, and control in order.

edge: Drive the output side while leaving the input undriven and verify the switch does not provide bidirectional transfer.
positive: Enable an nmos and propagate a source value from input to output.

edge: Place a gate delay before a net delay and distinguish the two propagation stages.
positive: Change a net driver and observe that the net update occurs after its net delay.

negative: Specify more than three delay values on a net.
positive: Use a legal three-value net delay specification.

edge: Use highz0 or highz1 as one component while the opposite component remains driven.
negative: Use a strength1 keyword as the strength0 component.
positive: Form strengths using one valid strength0 and one valid strength1 component.

edge: Use an unknown transition whose delay is selected by the minimum rule at both arities.
positive: Compare otherwise identical two-input and many-input gates with the same delay specification and verify equal transition delay.

edge: Cause a transition to x and verify it uses the smaller of distinct rise and fall delays.
negative: Supply three delay values to an and gate.
positive: Give an and gate distinct rise and fall delays and observe each output transition.

edge: Combine x or z with a controlling input for and/nand and or/nor, then compare with xor/xnor where unknown propagates.
positive: Exercise controlling and noncontrolling 0/1 combinations for each gate family.

edge: Distinguish the keyword `or` from use of an operator expression in an input terminal.
negative: Use buf as a multiple-input logic-gate primitive.
positive: Declare each of the six multiple-input gate primitive types.

edge: Exercise controlling and unknown values beyond the first two inputs.
positive: Compare a three-input gate result with the corresponding reduction over all three values.

edge: Use the minimum legal one-input form for each multiple-input gate keyword.
negative: Instantiate an and gate with no input terminal or with two output terminals.
positive: Instantiate an and gate with one output and one input, and another with several inputs.

edge: Cause a transition to x and verify the smaller of distinct rise and fall delays is used.
negative: Supply three delay values to a not gate.
positive: Give a buf gate distinct rise and fall delays and observe each output transition.

edge: Declare the minimum one-output form and a several-output form for each keyword.
negative: Use and as a multiple-output primitive with several outputs.
positive: Declare both buf and not primitive instances.

edge: Use the minimum one-output, one-input form.
negative: Place the input first or provide multiple input terminals to not.
positive: Instantiate buf with several outputs followed by one input.

edge: Toggle a controlled switch between enabled and disabled while opposite-side drivers are present.
positive: Pass a signal in each direction through tran and through an enabled tranif.

edge: Compare rtranif0 and tranif0 declarations differing only in resistive behavior.
negative: Use nmos with a bidirectional pass-switch terminal form.
positive: Declare each unconditional, controlled, resistive, and nonresistive pass-switch keyword.

negative: Connect rtran to a whole vector net or a user-defined net.
positive: Connect a resistive pass switch to scalar nets and to vector-net bit-selects.

negative: Connect tran between two different user-defined net types.
Connect tran between a user-defined net and a built-in net.

edge: Compare the same declaration using rtran, which does not admit user-defined net terminals.
positive: Connect tran between two nets of the same user-defined net type.

edge: Verify resistive pass switches preserve small charge and high impedance.
notes: Use built-in nets and hold control/conduction constant.
positive: Propagate ordinary and supply strengths through tran or tranif and verify preservation versus supply-to-strong.
Propagate strong, pull, and medium-charge signals through rtran or rtranif and verify table reductions.

edge: Distinguish zero through-delay from a nonzero control turn-on delay.
positive: With an already-enabled tranif, change a value on one side and observe immediate propagation to the other side.

edge: Use a one-element range, which remains an array declaration and therefore requires a name.
negative: Give an unnamed primitive instance an array range.
positive: Declare one unnamed scalar gate and one named gate-instance array.

edge: Use one keyword for a declaration containing several instances and verify no per-instance primitive keyword is accepted.
negative: Place an instance identifier before the primitive keyword.
positive: Begin a declaration with a valid gate keyword followed by two comma-separated instances of that gate type.

edge: Use a bidirectional switch whose two inout terminals occupy the leading terminal positions.
negative: Place an input terminal before the gate's output terminal.
positive: Declare an and gate with output first followed by comma-separated input expressions in parentheses.

edge: Use distinct expressions for all three members.
negative: Supply a malformed two-member colon delay control.
positive: Use literal and parameter-expression min:typ:max triples in procedural delay controls.

edge: Declare each pull primitive with a two-strength pair.
negative: Declare pullup with only a strength0 keyword.
positive: Declare pullup with one strength1 keyword and pulldown with one strength0 keyword.
Compare pullup with explicit strong1 and pulldown with explicit strong0 against their defaults.

edge: Declare multiple pull instances in one declaration with a shared strength specification.
negative: Use supply1 as though it were a pull primitive keyword.
positive: Declare both pullup and pulldown sources.

edge: Resolve a pull source against another driver to distinguish driven value and strength.
positive: Connect pullup and pulldown separately to undriven nets and observe 1 and 0.

negative: Attach a delay specification to either pull source.
positive: Declare pullup and pulldown without delays.
Use two-member pull strength pairs and vary only pullup strength0 or pulldown strength1; verify the driven strength is unchanged.
Observe the default strength of otherwise undriven pullup and pulldown nets.

edge: Verify both supply and strong collapse to pull, while small charge and high impedance remain unchanged.
positive: Pass every input strength class through a resistive switch and compare the output mapping.

edge: Compare the paired 0 and 1 names at each equal numeric level.
positive: Create representative values at each named strength and inspect their numeric ordering through standardized strength observations.

edge: Reverse textual pair order while retaining one keyword from each value domain.
negative: Pair two strength1-domain keywords as though one were strength0.
positive: Use each listed strength1 and strength0 keyword in a valid pair.

edge: Resolve equal opposing strengths to x and verify both 0 and 1 portions contribute.
positive: Create resolved known 0, known 1, x, and z net states and inspect their value/strength representation.

edge: Compare with tri0 and tri1 implicit pull strengths.
positive: Resolve supply0 and supply1 against weaker opposite-value drivers and observe supply dominance.

edge: Exercise x-to-z, z-to-x, and transitions out of x or z.
positive: Use distinct d1, d2, and d3 and exercise every tabled from-to transition.

edge: Add a stronger opposite-value driver and verify it overrides the implicit pull.
positive: Leave tri0 and tri1 otherwise undriven and observe pull-strength 0 and 1.

edge: Re-enable a driver just before decay expiry and verify the pending decay ends without changing the new driven value to x.
positive: Release a charged 0 or 1 and observe x exactly after the decay time.

edge: Compare weak driving strength level 3 with medium charge level 2 during resolution.
negative: Attempt to use a charge-storage strength as an ordinary gate drive-strength keyword.
positive: Use trireg nets with large, medium, and small charge strengths and observe stored-value resolution.

edge: Use no decay delay and distinguish indefinite retention from initial z.
positive: Drive trireg to 0, 1, and x separately, then drive z and verify each value is retained until decay or a new active drive.

edge: Compare omitted strength with explicit medium.
negative: Specify a non-charge driving strength as trireg storage strength.
positive: Charge trireg nets declared with large, medium, small, and omitted strengths, then release the driver and inspect stored strength.

edge: Use zero rise/fall with nonzero decay.
negative: Attempt to specify charge-decay time without both preceding rise and fall delays.
positive: Declare distinct rise, fall, and decay values and observe each event.

edge: Release active drivers to z after storing 0 or 1 and verify z does not replace the stored value.
positive: Observe initial trireg z and force an already-charged trireg to z.

edge: Cause a transition to x and verify the minimum applicable delay is selected.
negative: Supply four delay values to a bufif gate.
positive: Specify three distinct delays and separately observe rising, falling, and transition-to-z output changes.

edge: Combine x and z control values with each of 0, 1, x, and z data to verify H, L, or x table outcomes.
notes: Where H or L permits either value, use a set-valued oracle.
positive: For each primitive, exercise enabled and disabled control with data 0 and 1.

edge: Compare bufif0 with bufif1 declarations while holding terminal shape constant.
negative: Use buf as though it were a controlled three-state primitive.
positive: Declare each of the four three-state primitive keywords.

edge: Use complex expressions for data and control while preserving terminal roles.
negative: Swap the data and control terminals or omit one terminal.
positive: Instantiate each three-state gate with output, data, and control in that order.

notes: Use a set-aware value oracle while comparing event times.
positive: Measure H, L, and x transitions under unequal gate delays and compare selected timing.

edge: Distinguish H and L from unrestricted x.
positive: Create an unknown-control combination yielding L or H and accept either member of its defined set.

edge: Compare equivalent drivers on a built-in resolved net and a user-defined nettype.
positive: Drive a user-defined nettype from sources carrying different strength annotations and verify its resolution function receives values without strength effects.

edge: Contrast with resistive reduction on built-in nets.
notes: User-defined nettypes do not themselves carry strength levels; observe the UDN resolution behavior without importing built-in strength semantics.
positive: Pass values through tran between same-type user-defined nets and verify resolution is not modified by switch strength reduction.

edge: Compare otherwise equivalent tranif connections using user-defined versus built-in net types under unknown control.
positive: Drive x and z controls on a tranif connecting same-type user-defined nets and verify the sides remain disconnected.

edge: Combine several same-value drivers including duplicate strengths and verify the greatest strength remains.
positive: Combine unequal opposing strengths and verify the strongest value and strength win.

negative: Attach a delay specification to tran or rtran.
positive: Declare tran and rtran without delays.

edge: Drive both terminals concurrently and observe bidirectional net resolution.
negative: Give tran a third control terminal.
positive: Instantiate tran with two nets and drive each side in separate scenarios.

edge: Use component pairs containing both equal and unequal strengths so dominance and wired logic both contribute.
positive: Combine two multi-level ambiguous signals on wand and wor and derive the result from every component pair.

edge: Include x or z drivers and apply the corresponding four-state logic function.
positive: Drive equal-strength 0 and 1 onto wand/triand and wor/trior nets and verify AND versus OR resolution at that strength.
